gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Anker's EverFrost 2 40L runs 52 h on its own 288 Wh battery: 288 Wh ÷ 52 h ≈ 5.5 W, or about 133 Wh a day, measured empty at 77 °F, Eco mode and 39 °F inside. That is one $899.99 box that gets through 48 h with only 4 h to spare. The other route, a Dometic CFX3 25 at its 90 °F rating, needs at least 624 Wh of rated station capacity for two days.
standout_why: I compared against willitrunpower.com (cited), our own page (cited), sparkpowered.com, poweroutageplanner.com and newworldsurvival.com. Willrun already works out DC runtimes for the Dometic CFX3 25 at 11.04 W on 768 Wh to 2 kWh stations, so that part isn't new. No page names the Anker EverFrost 2 or its 52 h figure on 288 Wh. None gives the minimum rated station size for exactly 48 h, and none includes the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, a 25 lb, 1,024 Wh unit. Sparkpowered covers only kitchen fridges and CPAP. Poweroutageplanner uses a generic 40–60 W fridge with no models. Newworldsurvival covers gel and evaporative coolers only.
decides: It backs the robust pick: a 1 kWh station on 12 V running a Dometic CFX3 25. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 is the lightest of these at 25 lb and gives about 79 h at Dometic's 90 °F rating, 31 h more than needed, for $1,198.99 together. It also adds a cheaper single-box option, the EverFrost 2 40L at $899.99. But that only clears 48 h at 77 °F with the cooler empty, so in a summer outage it needs a second power source. A 288 Wh station is not enough with the Dometic: the Elite 30 V2 gives about 22 h.
